map.rationale: The recessed wall panels between the piers show irregular, mottled, multi-tone grey rubble with no coursing — rough cobblestone masonry, distinct from the smooth dressed piers framing them.

map.role: buttress piers, quoins and opening frames
map.rationale: The vertical piers, corner quoins and door jambs read as crisp, regular rectangular blocks with clean mortar lines — dressed stone-brick, deliberately smoother and lighter than the cobblestone fields they border (the near-tone grey pair to preserve).
A continuous dressed-stone banding course with a chamfered cap wraps the foot of all walls — the same crisp coursed masonry as the piers, set as the earth-bound base.
The two steep roof planes are deep red-brown horizontal plank courses — the dark dominant timber mass, clearly distinct in value from the warmer door wood.

The two cart openings are filled with bright, warm golden-orange vertical boarding — markedly lighter and warmer than the dark roof, a separate oak timber kept distinct from the dark_oak planes above.

entry.rationale: The roof oversails the wall on a crisp stepped lip at the eave line — a dark_oak stair course giving the overhang its shadow edge, same timber family as the roof field.
